title: Console Release Notes — 2026-04: Usage Insights (Cost Drivers by Route + Model)
author: Paula Mendes
body:
## Summary
This release introduces **Usage Insights: Cost Drivers by Route**, a first-class console experience to help engineering and ops teams quickly answer:
- Which routes/endpoints cost the most?
- Which models (and model variants) drive spend on those routes?
- What changed week-over-week (or vs a prior period)?

Usage Insights is designed for **FinOps/chargeback workflows**, performance triage, and ongoing cost optimization.

---

## What’s new
### 1) Route list: top cost drivers
A new console view surfaces route-level spend ranked by total cost, with quick filters and trend sparklines.

**Available metrics by route (time window selectable):**
- **Cost:** total cost, input tokens, output tokens, cached tokens (where applicable), unit cost (where applicable)
- **Performance:** p50/p95 latency, error rate
- **Breakdowns/filters:** environment, region, org/project, deployment mode, model

### 2) Route detail: model breakdown + “what changed”
Selecting a route opens a detail view showing:
- **Spend and token breakdown by model** (including model variants when applicable)
- **Deltas vs prior period** (e.g., last 7 days vs previous 7 days)
- Context for interpreting changes (e.g., shifts in token mix, changes in model selection)

### 3) Exportable reports (CSV + JSON) with audit logging
You can export a bounded Usage Insights report suitable for attaching to:
- monthly spend reviews
- internal incident/cost write-ups
- chargeback allocation and finance workflows

**Export behavior:**
- Supports **CSV and JSON**
- Export requests are **RBAC-scoped** to your org/project boundaries
- Export creation and download actions are **audit logged** (who/when/filters/time window)

---

## Availability / rollout
- Rollout is **staged** and controlled via feature flag.
- Hosted API + Dedicated customers will be enabled first; Private deployments follow per release train and deployment schedule.
- Data appears once route/model telemetry is present (see “Required customer actions”).

If you are a design partner or need early access for a finance workflow, contact your CSM or open a support ticket referencing **“Usage Insights: Cost Drivers by Route”**.

---

## Required customer actions
Usage Insights depends on a stable `route` identifier. To get accurate route-level attribution, customers must tag requests with a route identifier (or ensure gateway route derivation is configured).

### Route tagging (recommended)
**Goal:** consistently label requests with a human-readable, low-cardinality route key (e.g., `chat.completions`, `support_rag.answer`, `agents.summarize`).

**Guidelines (high level):**
- Use a small, stable set of route names (avoid dynamic values like user IDs, email addresses, document IDs)
- Prefer `.` or `/` separators; keep names short and consistent
- Treat route identifiers like metric dimensions: keep cardinality under control

### SDK and gateway support
- Redwood SDKs support setting a route identifier per request.
- Gateways can optionally derive a route from the inbound request path when configured.

**Docs:**
- Route tagging: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/usage-insights/route-tagging
- Usage Insights overview: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/usage-insights/overview

---

## Data behavior and limitations (known constraints)
### 1) Freshness vs accuracy
Usage Insights is designed to be near-real-time, but some cost attribution fields may arrive late.
- Expect the dashboard to be **fresh within minutes** for most traffic.
- Some totals may **settle** after late-arriving metering events are processed.

### 2) Invoice reconciliation
Usage Insights is optimized for operational decisions (top drivers and trends). It may not exactly match invoice totals due to:
- timing windows and late-arriving events
- rounding differences
- retention windows and report bounding

If you need invoice reconciliation, use invoice exports for billing totals and use Usage Insights for route/model allocation and change detection.

### 3) “Unknown route” bucket
If requests are not tagged (and gateway derivation is not configured), they will roll up under **Unknown route**. This can dominate top drivers until tagging is deployed.

### 4) Cardinality guardrails
To protect platform performance and avoid runaway metric dimensions, route values are subject to normalization and limits.
- Overly long or invalid route strings may be normalized.
- Excessive unique routes may be rolled up or truncated per guardrails.

### 5) Multi-model routing/fallback attribution
When smart routing selects a different model mid-flight (capacity fallback or policy routing), the system attributes spend to:
- the **original route**
- the **actual model(s) used** in the model breakdown

In rare edge cases during partial failures, model attribution may be incomplete while route totals remain present.

---

## Export limits (current)
Exports are intentionally bounded to protect performance and ensure predictable completion times.
- Maximum time range: limited in-console (varies by org tier)
- Maximum rows/file size: bounded; larger ranges require narrower filters or smaller windows
- Export jobs may fail for extremely broad queries; adjust filters/time range and retry

**Audit logging:** export creation and download are recorded in the audit log for compliance evidence.

Docs: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/usage-insights/exports

---

## Security / RBAC
Usage Insights and exports respect org/project scoping and role permissions.
- Users can only view and export data they have access to.
- Export audit events include the actor, time window, applied filters, and resource scope.

If you are running a security review, reference the audit logging documentation and request the export audit event schema from your CSM.

---

## Support and troubleshooting
### Common symptoms
- **Top drivers show “Unknown route”**: route tagging not yet deployed or gateway derivation not configured.
- **Route totals differ from invoice**: expected; see “Invoice reconciliation” section.
- **Export job times out**: narrow time range, add filters (project, region), or export JSON and post-process.

### Where to get help
- Docs: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/usage-insights
- Support: file a ticket with “Usage Insights” + affected org/project, time window, and export job ID (if applicable)

---

## Coming next (not in this release)
- Automated anomaly detection and alerting beyond basic “change vs prior period” views
- Customer-configurable custom dimensions beyond route/model
- Long-term historical exports beyond retention policy

---

## Internal notes (for launch coordination)
- Ensure release comms includes route tagging callout and screenshot updates.
- CS enablement: provide a short explanation for invoice mismatches and Unknown route guidance.
- SRE: confirm dashboards and alerts are green before expanding feature flag rollout.
